macro: US equity indices are mixed at midday with the S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq up 38 basis points, Russell 2000 up 30 basis points, and the Dow down 43 basis points. Investors are in a wait-and-see mode around UN activity regarding Iran and the Middle East, with Brent crude off modestly on hopes for a diplomatic resolution and news that Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline may be coming back online. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all dipping slightly while Treasuries are flat across the curve.
rates_fed: Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve with no major rate or Fed catalyst driving action today. The macro focus remains on geopolitical developments — specifically Iran offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases military pressure. No Fed speakers or data releases are driving rates today.
market_outlook: Adam's tone is cautiously neutral with a mild bullish lean into AI catalysts over the next week and a half. The key catalyst to watch is Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, followed by OpenAI's DevDay on September 29 and Micron earnings on September 30 — this cluster of AI events is keeping tech bid even as financials and defensives drag.
bull_case: AI enthusiasm is building ahead of a dense catalyst calendar including Meta Connect, OpenAI DevDay, and Micron earnings — and Meta's Muse agent is seeing surging downloads with Shopify integration adding real monetization optionality. Housing stocks, auto parts retailers, travel and leisure, and consumer staples are all showing relative strength, suggesting underlying breadth. Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz and the partial resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline could ease energy market tensions and remove a macro overhang.
bear_case: Financials are broadly underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers, and managed care are all under pressure, which is a meaningful headwind for the equal-weight index and reflects concern about the macro backdrop. Lab testing names Quest and LabCorp are getting hit on larger-than-expected CMS Medicare rate cuts, a reminder of regulatory earnings risk. Trump's approval rating has sunk to a career low of 32%, and political uncertainty around mid-terms — including GOP calls to ban diesel exports — adds a layer of policy unpredictability.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO impact. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus expectations of +3.1%, though management noted positive sales linearity through the quarter. The stock is rallying as traders focus on the linearity commentary and the comp trend rather than the headline miss.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and critically the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind still leaves EPS of 42 cents versus the 36-cent consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged. Solid quality beat in a tough environment.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% consensus. Revenue was actually slightly above at $2.311 billion versus $2.17 billion expected, but margin weakness dominated and management called out a difficult macro landscape. A weak result with forward visibility limited.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Connect keynote Wednesday night at 7pm ET, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform — a meaningful agentic commerce win. Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform, creating a competitive fault line. Investor expectations are growing more bullish into the event.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases directly on its e-commerce platform, giving it a potential edge over Amazon which has blocked Muse. This positions Shopify as a preferred agentic commerce partner at a critical moment in the AI agent wars. Bullish for Shopify's relevance in the emerging agentic shopping ecosystem.

Quest and LabCorp shares were hit Tuesday following new Medicare payment rates from CMS for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. This is a direct earnings headwind with limited ability to offset on the cost side. Both names are underperforming meaningfully on the news.

LabCorp is under pressure alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS released new Medicare lab service payment rates that were worse than expected. The rate cuts are a direct top-line and margin headwind for the lab testing industry. Sentiment on both names has turned decidedly negative.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the trial. This is a meaningful clinical milestone that keeps Viking competitive in the increasingly crowded but high-value GLP-1 obesity drug space. The data supports continued bull thesis on the name.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense — described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI — for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. This is a strategic bet on the Physical AI and robotics wave and expands Cognex's capabilities meaningfully. Deal size is notable relative to Cognex's scale.

On Holdings held its analyst meeting and outlined a 2029 sales target of at least CHF 5.6 billion versus the Street at CHF 5.4 billion, with EBITDA margins of 22% or better versus consensus at 21%. The company also adopted a $1 billion buyback authorization. Targets above consensus with capital return added is a clean bullish setup.

sectors: Financials broadly underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers, and managed care all weak. Lab testing hit by CMS rate cuts. AI and semiconductors outperforming with ARM, ASML, GOOGL, META, MU, ORCL among leaders. Housing (DHI, LEN, PHM), auto parts retail (AZO, ORLY, GPC), travel/leisure, and consumer staples showing strength. Aerospace and defense broadly lower. Data center sentiment cooling after Texas Governor Abbott ordered a halt to new data center permitting, and SB Energy delayed its IPO after investors balked at its $50 billion-plus valuation target.

tts_summary: Here's your midday market update for Tuesday, September 22nd. Markets are in a holding pattern. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, but the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is off fractionally around a hundred dollars a barrel as traders digest two competing Middle East headlines — Iran reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps toward easing military pressure, and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline appears to be at least partially coming back online after Houthi and Iraq militia disruptions forced the Saudis back through Hormuz. The geopolitical read is cautiously constructive on energy supply, which is why crude is off. The bigger market story right now is AI anticipation. Investors are positioning into a very dense catalyst window — Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote tomorrow night at seven pm Eastern, followed by OpenAI's DevDay on the 29th and Micron earnings on the 30th. That's keeping pockets of tech bid. On individual names — AutoZone beat on earnings but it was low quality, driven by tariff refunds and a LIFO accounting benefit, while domestic comps missed badly at plus 1.6 versus the 3.1 the Street expected. The stock is rallying because management said comp linearity was positive through the quarter, meaning the trend improved. MillerKnoll was a genuine beat — 53 cents versus 36 expected, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind they still cleared the bar at 42 cents. THOR Industries missed, with gross margins down 230 basis points year-over-year, and management flagged a difficult macro environment. Viking Therapeutics is a bright spot — positive phase trial data on their GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed 22 percent weight loss. Meta continues to build momentum into tomorrow's keynote with surging Muse agent downloads and a new Shopify integration that lets Muse complete purchases directly on Shopify's platform — Amazon blocked Muse, which makes Shopify's move strategically significant. Cognex is acquiring RealSense, the leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly 500 million dollars upfront. On Holdings raised its 2029 targets above Street and added a one billion dollar buyback. On the bearish side — Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp are getting hit hard after CMS released Medicare lab payment rates that were worse than the market expected. Financials broadly are underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers, and managed care are all lower. Data center sentiment is also wobbling — Texas has now halted new permitting for data centers, and SB Energy pulled back its IPO after investors balked at the fifty billion dollar-plus valuation. Directionally, the tape feels rangebound until tomorrow night's Meta keynote gives AI a direction to run. Watch crude and Hormuz headlines as a secondary macro driver.
